column2: Louis Pasteur boiled broth in flasks with S-shaped necks: air got in, but dust and microbes stuck in the bend, so the broth stayed sterile. It helped kill off the idea of spontaneous generation.
Invented by Franz von Soxhlet in 1879 to extract fat from solid samples. It sounds wonderfully obscure, but most organic chemistry students have watched one siphon away for hours.
